headline: Medium prompt-injection and cascading-error risk: pdf.js can parse attacker-controlled PDFs while LlamaFactory has no isolation or verification path.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: pdf.js ingests PDF files by default, and LlamaFactory has no documented isolation, provenance tracking, or input-verification surface. If pdf.js output is forwarded into LlamaFactory prompts or training data, attacker-controlled PDF text can steer instructions. The pairwise pathway is inferred from documented file handling, not directly reproduced.
conditions: IF pdf.js output is copied into LlamaFactory prompts or datasets
IF the PDF source is attacker-controlled
IF no provenance filter strips instruction-like text
mitigations: Require manual review of extracted text before reuse
Strip imperative phrases from PDF-derived text
Use a separate staging workspace for PDF extraction
Disable any auto-ingest from pdf.js into LlamaFactory
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between extraction and downstream use

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents are documented as network-egress none, and neither profile shows secrets handling or shared authenticated services. pdf.js touches PDF documents, while LlamaFactory has no filesystem read/write or clipboard surfaces. A leakage path is therefore limited to unusual operator-mediated copying rather than default exfiltration.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies PDF contents into LlamaFactory
IF sensitive data is present in the PDFs
IF a separate export channel is introduced outside the profiles
mitigations: Keep sensitive PDFs out of shared manual workflows
Use redacted sample PDFs for testing
Confirm both agents remain offline
Avoid copying extracted text into prompts
requires-engineering: add DLP checks on any export path

C_capability_conflict.rationale: LlamaFactory cannot write the filesystem, modify git state, or spawn subprocesses, while pdf.js supports browser-based tests and multiple instances. There is no documented overlapping write authority to the same mutable resource, so direct capability conflict is unlikely. Uncertainty is low because the profiles explicitly block the main conflict surfaces.
conditions: IF LlamaFactory is wrapped by an external orchestrator that grants write access
IF both agents are given the same mutable workspace by another system
mitigations: Keep LlamaFactory read-only
Run pdf.js in an isolated browser profile
Separate work directories per agent
Avoid shared git worktrees
requires-engineering: add workspace locks in the orchestrator

D_cascading_error.rationale: pdf.js can produce extracted document text, and LlamaFactory is a general LLM/fine-tuning tool that may treat upstream text as training or prompt material. If the extracted content is accepted without verification, errors or malicious instructions can cascade into downstream outputs. The interaction is plausible from the profiles, but not directly documented.
conditions: IF pdf.js extraction is used as authoritative input to LlamaFactory
IF no human verification step checks the extracted text
IF downstream outputs are generated from that text
mitigations: Add a verification step before reuse
Compare extracted text against the source PDF
Limit downstream use to non-authoritative drafts
Flag low-confidence OCR or extraction artifacts
requires-engineering: implement source-to-output traceability

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, retention, or subject-rights mismatch is documented for either agent. The only concrete compliance-relevant data class is pdf documents in pdf.js, while LlamaFactory lists no touched data classes or secrets. Because the pairwise compliance pathway is undocumented, the risk is limited to policy gaps introduced by the operator.
conditions: IF regulated content such as PHI or EU PII is placed into PDF files
IF the operator routes those PDFs into a non-compliant downstream process
IF retention or deletion policies differ in the surrounding workflow
mitigations: Classify PDFs before processing
Keep regulated PDFs out of test workflows
Document retention for extracted text
Verify local policy for any downstream storage
requires-engineering: map data flows to residency and retention controls
